title: Assembling LED Controller Electronics
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdiai4ae

steps.title: Solder SMD components
steps.instruction: Using a thin solder wire, solder flux and watchmaker's tweezers, solder all surface‑mount devices (SMDs) highlighted in red on the board before any through‑hole parts.

steps.title: Add power supply and test
steps.instruction: Solder the DC power jack (J1), toggle switch (SW1), fuse holder (F1) and insert a 1.25 A fuse; then verify the partial circuit by measuring the expected voltages with a digital multimeter.

substeps.instruction: Solder connector J1, switch SW1, and fuse holder F1 onto the PCB.
Insert a 1.25 A fuse into the fuse holder.
Connect a +30 V power supply to the DC jack (J1).
Set the multimeter to DC‑Voltage mode.
Place the black (ground) probe on test point GND1 and the red probe on +1.25 V; the reading should be ≈1.25 V.
If the reading is off, re‑inspect solder joints; replace shunt reference D1 (MAX6006) if it is faulty.
Toggle SW1 to the opposite position.
Place the black probe on GND2 and the red probe on +30 V; the reading should be ≈30 V.
If the reading is off, re‑inspect solder joints; replace Q1 if it is damaged.
Do not continue until both voltage checks are successful.

steps.title: Install LED current regulation
steps.instruction: Mount the rotary‑switch circuitry, add the jumper header, and verify that the output voltage steps correctly with each switch position.

substeps.instruction: Solder the 3‑way header (JP1) onto the board.
Insert a jumper shunt across the two lower pins of JP1 (labelled INT).
Solder a DIP‑8 socket for the rotary switch (SW2) – do NOT solder the switch itself yet.
Solder a 3‑pin header adjacent to JP1.
Insert a jumper shunt into the lower two pins of the 3‑pin header.
Place the 6‑position rotary switch into the DIP‑8 socket.
Reconnect the +30 V supply to J1.
With the switch in each position, measure the voltage between test points GND and VAR:
• Position 0 → 1.25 V
• Position 1 → 1.09 V
• Position 2 → 0.93 V
• Position 3 → 0.78 V
• Position 4 → 0.62 V
• Position 5 → 0.46 V
• Position 6 → 0.30 V
If any voltage deviates significantly, re‑check solder joints and measure SMD resistor values; repair any loose joints or misplaced components.
If no voltage is present, confirm the jumper shunt on JP1 is correctly placed.
Do not proceed until all voltage steps are verified.

steps.title: Add LED controller components
steps.instruction: Solder the adjustable LED driver (DC1) and screw‑terminal connectors J2 through J7, completing the through‑hole assembly.

substeps.instruction: Solder the adjustable LED driver (DC1) into its footprint.
Solder screw‑terminal connectors J2, J3, J4, J5, J6 and J7.
Verify that all through‑hole parts are securely soldered.
Do NOT power the circuit with LEDs yet; the LED strip will be mounted on the heatsink later.

steps.title: Clean PCB
steps.instruction: Remove all flux residues from the assembled board using isopropanol (IPA) and a soft brush.

substeps.instruction: Obtain a small tub (e.g., an old margarine tub) that fits the PCB and can be sealed with a lid.
Place the PCB in the tub and cover it with isopropanol (the board does not need to be fully submerged).
Close the lid and let the board soak for at least 10 minutes (overnight soaking is optional).
Using a toothbrush and a toothpick, scrub the board to dislodge flux deposits.
Dispose of the used solvent according to local waste‑disposal regulations.
Refill the tub with fresh isopropanol, reseal, and soak for an additional 10 minutes.
Brush again to remove any remaining flux.
Tilt or flick the board to remove excess solvent and allow it to air‑dry completely.
